best_hook.why: A bride in a mud-soaked wedding gown marching into the rain saying 'at least no one there will be waiting to humiliate me' hints at a public disgrace; it is the only line with any edge.

best_cliffhanger.why: Cutting on 'I am.' right after 'You are not disappointed?' leaves her answer sounding like a rejection of her scarred husband, before 'But not because of you' softens it.

must_promos.why: Least bad cut: the humiliation line and the rain-soaked bride set up a riches-to-rags story, the leaking hovel and 'This is all I can give you now' raise the stakes, and the edit cuts on her admitting she is disappointed.

standalone_risk: There is no antagonist on screen; a stranger does not learn who humiliated her, why she married this man, or that he is secretly more than he seems, so the clip reads as a mood piece rather than a conflict.
notes: A quiet, cosy transition episode. The only conflict is implied (her lost home and her humiliation). The cliffhanger is manufactured by cutting before she reassures him.
